[[File:CalafateFlower.jpg|thumb|Calafate flower]]
'''''Berberis microphylla''''', common name '''box-leaved barberry'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17}}</ref> and '''Magellan barberry''',<ref name=PFAF>{{citation |url=http://www.pfaf.org/user/plant.aspx?LatinName=Berberis+buxifolia |title=Plants for a Future entry for ''Berberis buxifolia'' Lam. |accessdate=3 January 2016}}</ref> in [[Spanish language|Spanish]] '''calafate''' and '''michay''' and other names,<ref>{{citation|title=''Berberis microphylla'' at FrutasdelBosque|url=https://frutasdelbosque.org/calafate/|language=es}}

</ref> is an evergreen shrub, with simple, shiny [[Buxus|box]]-like leaves. The calafate is native to southern [[Argentina]] and [[Chile]] and is a symbol of [[Patagonia]].<ref>Ahrendt, L. W. A. (1961). ''Berberis'' and ''Mahonia''. A taxonomic revision. J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 57(369): 1–410.</ref><ref>Landrum, L. R. 1999 [2000]. Revision of ''Berberis'' (Berberidaceae) in Chile and adjacent southern Argentina. Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 86(4): 793–834.</ref><ref>Hoffmann, A. (1982). Flora silvestre de Chile zona araucana. Edición 4. Ediciones Fundación Claudio Gay, Santiago, Chile. 258p.</ref><ref>Landrum, L. R. (2003). Berberidaceae. En C. Marticorena y R. Rodríguez [eds.], Flora de Chile Vol. 2(2), pp 1–23. Universidad de Concepción, Concepción.</ref><ref>Marticorena, C. & M. Quezada. (1985). Catálogo de la Flora Vascular de Chile. Gayana, Bot. 42: 1–157.</ref><ref>Zuloaga, F. O. (1997). Catálogo de las plantas vasculares de la Argentina. Monogr. Syst. Bot. Missouri Bot. Gard. 74(1–2): 1–1331.</ref>
''Berberis microphylla'' should not be confused with ''[[Mahonia microphylla]]'', native to [[China]].<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=250096506 Flora of China Vol. 19 Page 778 <big>小叶十大功劳</big> xiao ye shi da gong lao ''Mahonia microphylla'' T. S. Ying & G. R. Long]</ref>
==Description==
The bush grows to a height of {{convert|1.0|to|1.5|m|0|abbr=on}}. It has many arching branches, each covered in many tripartite spines. The bush has many small yellow flowers in summer. It produces blue-black berries.
==Uses==
[[File:Calafate-Berberis buxifolia 02.jpg|right|thumb|Fruits in spring]]
Its edible blue-black [[Berry (botany)|berries]] are harvested for [[jam]]s, but are eaten fresh too - a legend tells that anyone who eats a calafate berry will be certain to return to Patagonia.<ref>{{Cite web|title=El que come calafate ha de volver|url=http://www.patagoniachilena.com/historia/leyenda-come-calate-volver/|url-status=dead|website=Patagoniachilena.com|language=es|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605192319/http://www.patagoniachilena.com/historia/leyenda-come-calate-volver/|archive-date=2011-06-05|access-date=2021-09-30}}</ref> It is also used as an additive in alcoholic beverages such as calafate beer.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lemoine |first=María Laura |last2=Fontana |first2=Ulises |last3=Hurtado |first3=Jazmín B. |last4=Pintos |first4=Federico M. |last5=Arena |first5=Miriam E. |last6=Vicente |first6=Ariel R. |last7=Rodoni |first7=Luis M. |date=2021-12-16 |title=WILD BARBERRY FRUIT (Berberis microphylla G. Forst.) AS A NATURAL INGREDIENT FOR BEER BREWING |url=https://revistas.udec.cl/index.php/chjaas/article/view/6424 |journal=Chilean Journal of Agricultural & Animal Sciences |language=en |volume=37 |issue=3 |pages=313–324 |doi=10.29393/CHJAAS37-32WBML70032 |issn=0719-3890|hdl=11336/164839 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> 

The calafate is grown commercially for its fruit, potential medical uses<ref name=PFAF/> and as a garden plant or [[bonsai]]. Its wood is used to make a red [[dye]]. The [[cultivar]] ''Berberis microphylla'' 'Nana' is widely available as a garden shrub, and is also used in commercial plantings as a low spiny hedge to discourage intruders, but it does not fruit.<ref>{{GRIN | ''Berberis heterophylla'' | 6872 | accessdate = November 17, 2007}}</ref>
